description: Linear A inscription translations, keyed by inscription id. Each entry gives the composite translation and a word-by-word analysis with readings, glosses and confidence.

dialect_notes.description: Two NWS sub-dialects attested in the libation formula corpus. Suffix variation is NOT free variation—it encodes genuine phonological differences between proto-Canaanite/Hebrew (standard, central/south Crete) and proto-Phoenician (Palaikastro, eastern Crete).
dialect_notes.chronological_significance: If the formula dates to MM III–LM IA (~1700–1500 BCE), this is the earliest attestation of the Canaanite dialect split—400+ years before the Ahiram inscription (Byblos, ~1000 BCE).
dialect_notes.decipherment_implication: Any proposed formula reading must yield valid NWS morphology in BOTH dialects simultaneously. This is a powerful constraint for testing candidates.

Vocative particle yā + proposed theonym Diqqitu. The written form is DI-KI-TU, and the group occupies the deity slot rather than a dedicant slot. Variant A-DI-KI-TE at Palaikastro.

√y-š-r. Adverbial accusative: *yaššaram* 'in righteousness.' Spelling encodes accusative -am (RA = /ra/, not RU for nominative -um). Polysemic layer: masculine divine name Yasharam (Akk. Mīšarum, Phoen. Misor). Position 3 in the full formula. On IO Za 2 only JA-SA-SA-RA-[ survives; GORILA restores ME (V 19).

U-NA is tentatively /wannā/ or /winnā/, comparing Ugaritic w hn beside contracted wn and Lipiński's *wa-hanna/u; it is translated here as 'so, behold.' KA-NA-SI = kanāsī 'my gathering' (G verbal noun of √k-n-s + 1cs -ī); Aramaic-shaped alternative knāšī; Syriac knšy 'gather!' (Peshitta Jer 10:17) is a verbal rival. On IO Za 2 only ]-SI survives; GORILA restores U-NA-KA-NA (V 19), read in full on KO Za 1 and SY Za 2.

IOZa2.translation: I make myself a dwelling—O Diqqitu!—in righteousness. So, behold my gathering in the presence of sacred song. May you be favorable toward us.
IOZa2.notes:
Context: Peak sanctuary libation formula—fullest attestation.

PRESERVATION: Five groups are fully preserved. Positions 3–4 are partly or largely restored: line 1 breaks after JA-SA-SA-RA- on face c and resumes with final -SI on face d; GORILA restores [ME · U-NA-KA-NA] from the parallel formulae (GORILA V, 19). The composite translation includes those editorial restorations and reads *301 as /na/: Kober triplets across 17 formula variants point to the verbal root n-w-y 'to dwell' (Ug. nawû, Heb. nāweh), substitution yields 9 independent NWS readings, and NA outperforms the rival r(V) value 9 to 2.

ANALYSIS: TA-NA-RA-TE-U-TI-NU is provisionally read from √r-ṣ-y, with analogical 2fs marking followed by a 1cp object; an n-extension remains the principal alternative. STRUCTURE: (1) invocation, positions 1–3; (2) presentation, positions 4–6, with wannā as the hinge and the gathering placed before sacred song; (3) petition, position 7. Diqqitu is compared with Astour's Diqet, the goat-goddess (Ugaritic dqt, √d-q-q; Astour 1966). Position 3 is translated adverbially as *yaššaram*, 'in righteousness'; a divine-name layer remains a secondary possibility.

FINAL BREAK: I-DA-[ is untranslated. It is not a standalone I: GORILA V, 18–19 reads I-DA-[, and Younger estimates a word of approximately six signs. Line 2 ends in the break on face c; face d line 2 is vacat. A related sequence follows the closing petition at Iouktas on IO Za 11 (]U-TI-NU · I-NA-I-DA-•[).

TLZa1.translation: I make myself a dwelling, O Sukar, in righteousness. So behold my gathering, [in the presence of sacred song].
TLZa1.notes: Context: Troullos peak-sanctuary libation formula on stone ladle HM 1545. The first four groups through U-NA-KA-NA-SI are preserved. Only NA-MA and SI-RU survive after the damaged interval; I-PI and final TE are formulaic restorations. O-SU-QA-RE is provisionally parsed as vocative ʾō + Sukar, with final E as the dead spelling vowel after /r/. Geʿez ʾo- supplies a later structural parallel for the vocative (Leslau 1987, 1), not proof of the Bronze Age form; the Egyptian Sokar identification remains CANDIDATE.

words.note: tG-stem middle-reflexive. Same formula verb as IOZa2.

Hapax. Vocative addressee in position two, as Sokar at Troullos and Dikte at Iouktas, before dubur ʾIda, 'the sanctuary of Ida.' √t-r-s 'to shield, protect' (Ar. turs; Lane 302); the shield-bearing Kouretes of Ida, and the Sea People Tursha (Egyptian twršꜣ), named from the same root (di Mino, Ya Diktu).

Preferred as a word-specific orthographic or graphic variant of DU-PU₂-RE, independently attested at PKZa15 and HTZb160. Facchetti (1999, 132) and Davis (2013, 44 n. 46) identify *314 here as a PU₂ variant; Thomas (2020, 8) presents the equation cautiously. Under di Mino's Semitic reading, dubur means 'sanctuary, inner sanctum' (√d-b-r). The equation does not assign PU₂ to every *314 attestation; the former du ḥōr(e) interpretation is withdrawn.

Preferred as the diptotic genitive in dubur ʾIda, 'the sanctuary of Ida': compare Ugaritic /ḥāmiyātu ʾugarita/, 'the walls of Ugarit' (Huehnergard 2012, §IV.B.3, p. 40). The older directive analysis 'toward Ida' remains possible, but Ugaritic writes that suffix with consonantal -h /-ah(a)/, so final A alone does not prove it.

U-NA is provisionally vocalized wannā 'and behold,' or, more naturally here, 'so, behold,' comparing Ugaritic w hn beside contracted wn and Lipiński's reconstruction *wa-hanna/u; the consonantal Ugaritic spelling does not determine the vowels. KA-NA-SI = kanāsī 'my gathering' (G verbal noun of √k-n-s + 1cs -ī); Aramaic-shaped alternative knāšī; Syriac knšy 'gather!' (Peshitta Jer 10:17) is a verbal rival.
√š-y-r 'sing': abstract šīrūt in -ūt (Ugaritic syllabic ši-i-ru /šīru/ 'song'); not šērūt 'service' (√š-r-t).

KOZa1.translation: I make myself a dwelling, O Tursa, Shield, in the sanctuary of Ida. So, behold my gathering in the presence of sacred song.
KOZa1.notes: TU-RU-SA occupies the formula's variable invocation slot and is therefore treated as a vocative addressee, not a dedicant. Preferred parse: DU-*314-RE is a word-specific variant of DU-PU₂-RE /dubur/ 'sanctuary' (PKZa15; HTZb160; Facchetti 1999, 132; Davis 2013, 44 n. 46; Thomas 2020, 8). I-DA-A is the diptotic genitive ʾIda, 'of Ida'; cf. Ugaritic /ḥāmiyātu ʾugarita/ 'the walls of Ugarit' (Huehnergard 2012, §IV.B.3, p. 40). U-NA is provisionally /wannā/, comparing Ugaritic w hn ~ wn and *wa-hanna/u; its exact vowels remain reconstructed. The former du ḥōr(e) is withdrawn; 'toward Ida' remains an alternative.

KO(?)Zf2.translation: [Untranslated continuous inscription; possibly contains the personal name Tōmar/Tamar.]
KO(?)Zf2.notes: GORILA IV 158–159 records a bronze bowl and prints all sixteen signs without dividers; the attribution KO(?) is uncertain. It is not independent evidence for a standalone noun nawā 'dwelling'.

DRAZg1.notes: Five-sign retrograde graffito from Drama-Kajrjaka, Bulgaria: DA-DU-*301̣-[?]-[?]. Fol and Schmitt compare only the first three signs with Linear A; the final two remain unread. RILA-S1 D 24 classifies the inscription as doubtful. DA-DU recurs initially in KN Zf 31 and HT 95. With *301 = /na/, /dādu-nā-/ 'our beloved …' is morphologically possible, but this is neither a complete word nor a secure prayer.

words.gloss: TI: May you (f.) answer; E: May she/you answer
words.note: GORILA classified the final form as an uncertain allograph of LA 37 TI; Ferrara, Montecchi, and Valério (2022, 87) reassign the PS Za 2.2 form to LA 38 E. PSZa2.translation: TI: ‘[…]—May you (f.) answer—[…]—in righteousness.’ E: ‘[…]—May she/you answer—[…]—in righteousness.’
PSZa2.notes: Fragmentary stone-vessel inscription from the Dictaean Cave. The initial ]-RE-I-KE and medial […]-JA-(TI/E) groups are incomplete and remain untranslated. With *301 = NA, TA-NA-I-*301-(TI/E) may be an N-stem of √ʿ-n-y 'answer,' structurally comparable with IOZa6. The sign traditionally read TI may instead be LA 38 E (Ferrara, Montecchi, and Valério 2022, 87). The TI reading permits di Mino's marked 2fs analysis; the E reading removes that marker and leaves TA- person-ambiguous. JA-SA-SA-RA-ME is read yaššaram, 'in righteousness.'

words.gloss: O Dikte, she of the Dubur
words.note: GORILA IV 34: A-DI-KI-TE-TE-[·] | [·]-RE, one lost sign at the end of side a and one at the start of side b; restored after PKZa15 JA-DI-KI-TE-TE-DU-PU₂-RE and PKZa8 JA-DI-KI-TE-TE-*307-PU₂-RE. The second TE stands only before dubur (PKZa8, PKZa15, PKZa11); the name alone has one dental (JA-DI-KI-TU, A-DI-KI-TE[, LB di-ka-ta-). TE = determinative de, cf. DU du; Ug. il d pid "El, the one of the heart" (KTU 1.4 IV 58–59). de CANDIDATE. Lit. "she of the Dubur": determinative + noun as a title, cf. Q 85:15 ذُو ٱلْعَرْشِ ḏū l-ʿarš "Owner of the Throne", Q 55:27 ذُو ٱلْجَلَٰلِ ḏū l-jalāl "Owner of Majesty", Nabataean ḏū-Šarā "Lord of the Shara." A- vocative as on PKZa12; Davis 2026 reads A- as "to/for".

DULAT 677 lists Ugaritic pṭry as a Semitic personal name; syllabic Ug. /piṭru/ 'loosening, release' and Amorite Annu-puṭri and Ištar-puṭri provide independent lexical and onomastic controls. Preferred here as the name qualified by A-KO-A-NE. Common-noun /piṭrī/ 'my release/opening,' a 2fs imperative 'release!,' and Pidray remain alternatives; Pidray requires TE = /d/. Rival: Gordon (1966, §124) reads . pi-te za . 'this engraved monument', Phoenician ptḥ z (KAI 10; Krahmalkov s.v. PTḤ III); the third sign stands between RI and ZA, but no divider follows TE.

Proposed singular title in apposition: PI-TE-RI A-KO-A-NE, 'Pitrī, the priest.' The root is secure (Ug. /kāhinu/, Heb. kōhēn, Phoenician khn), but the Canaanite article, exact vowels, and underrepresented /h/ remain reconstructed. The former plural vocative is withdrawn: Hebrew kōhănê is construct plural and Ugaritic has /kāhinūma/.
Standalone A between dividers. Best explained as line-split of A-SA-SA-RA-ME (cf. KNZa10 JA-SA-SA-RA-MA parallel). Alternatively: interjection or article.

words.gloss: uprightly (accusative -am, √y-š-r; Palaikastro dialect drops JA- prefix)
words.note: √y-š-r. Dialect variant: SA-SA-RA-ME (no JA- prefix) vs standard JA-SA-SA-RA-ME. Adverbial accusative *yaššaram* 'in righteousness.' Polysemic layer: masculine divine name Yasharam (Akk. Mīšarum, Phoen. Misor). Palaikastro proto-Phoenician dialect feature — cf. PKZa27 which retains JA- (standard register).

words.reading: wannā lū kanasti / winnā lū kanasti
words.note: U-NA /wannā/ 'so, behold' + RU /lū/ 'may' + KA-NA-TI /kanasti/, 2fs suffix form of √k-n-s 'gather' (di Mino, Ya Diktu). KA-NA-TI is indexed separately: the coda /s/ is unwritten before /t/, as Linear B drops syllable-final s before a stop (Ventris & Chadwick 1956, 45; pa-ka-na /phasgana/). Rivals: a feminine collective */kanast/* 'may there be a gathering' (compare later Hebrew kəneset 'assembly', Syriac knuštā); /qānastī/ 'I gathered' (Eccl 2:8).
√p-n-m. Expanded analytic spelling exclusive to Palaikastro (-MI-NA for standard -MA).
√š-y-r 'to sing' (Heb šīr, Exod 15:1). GORILA IV 34: SI-RU-[·], a lost third sign, not a truncation; SI-RU-[TE] as in the formula is possible (GORILA: SI-RU-DU not excluded).

Compound: I-NA (hinna 'behold!' presentative, the h unwritten; Hebrew hinnēh, Ugaritic hn; Arabic ʾinna is the later ʾ-form) + JA-PA-QA (3ms yaqtul √p-q-ḥ 'to open eyes,' Isa 42:7—guttural ḥ drops, explaining the 3-sign spelling with no missing radical). Theophanic epiphany closure of the PKZa11 prayer. Alt.: ʾina 'when' (cf. Akk. ina) + √p-q-d 'to visit'—'when he visits.' JA-PA-QA attested independently on PKZa12.

PKZa11.translation: I, Pitrī the priest, make myself a dwelling—O Dikte, Mistress of the Dubur—in righteousness. So, behold, may you gather! In the presence of song… […] …Behold, he opens (his eyes)!
PKZa11.notes:
Context: Peak sanctuary libation formula—longest liturgical inscription (11 words, 25 signs). Palaikastro dialect.

Complete 11-word liturgical inscription—longest in the corpus. The surface order is opening verb → invoked deity and title → proposed speaker's name and priestly title → adverbial formula element → standard body → lacuna → unique closure. Davis (2013, 42–43) and Thomas (2020, 8–10) independently place PI-TE-RI A-KO-A-NE in the subject/dedicant slot, though they infer two names rather than a name plus title. Reading the pair as 'Pitrī, the priest' supplies the explicit subject of the first-person opening without the former unattested 'first-offering' or unsupported plural vocative. The lacuna between SI-RU and I-NA-JA-PA-QA separates the formula from a masculine verbal closure whose subject remains unnamed.

words.gloss: And behold, may [there be] my gathering!

An isolated preserved JA between lacunae; it does not establish a relative pronoun or a word boundary.

Complete final group, also attested after I-NA on PK Za 11. Proto-Semitic *paqaḥ- and Hebrew/Aramaic √p-q-ḥ mean ‘open (the eyes).’ The omitted final laryngeal and masculine ya- keep the reading provisional.

PKZa12.translation: I make myself a dwelling—[Dikte … sacred song? … in righteousness? …]—and behold, may [there be] my gathering … [he opens (his eyes)?].
PKZa12.notes: Fragmentary libation table. Sides b–d contain substantial losses; restorations are formula-guided and remain bracketed. SI and RA-ME belong to separate damaged groups, plausibly SI-RU-[TE] and [A-SA-SA]-RA-ME. The diplomatic U-NA-RU-KA-[?]-JA-SI is normalized as U-NA-RU-KA-[NA]-(JA)-SI: the paradigm predicts KA-NA-SI, while JA is retained as a probable scribal intrusion. The damaged coda cannot securely yield ‘the servant who is appointed’; only final JA-PA-QA is complete enough for a lexical candidate.

words.note: One group on the tablet (GORILA I 141). Ug. åsr 'prisoner, captive' (DULAT 111); Akk. asīru 'captive used as worker', a western administrative word, with rations for the prisoner compound (CAD A/2 331–32). Rival: A + SA-RA₂ 'concerning the queen' (aššum, Huehnergard 2008: 285, 399).
*307-PU₂-RE (PK Za 8) = DU-PU₂-RE (PK Za 15).

Its position in the five-entry sum and its distribution in other personnel lists establish a personnel category. The former acrophonic DABBĀḤŪ 'sacrificers' reading is circular and has no phonetic complement here. Uchitel 2006, 75 instead proposes an age group.

SigLA analyzes the written unit as one composite sign, A542. Its components cannot be assumed to supply phonetic /lu...qe/. The former LUQḤU 'receipts/offerings' reading is therefore withdrawn for HT89.
'Water' (DULAT 529); under *307 dubur, the sanctuary's water-drawers (Josh 9:27). Rival: Uchitel 2006, 75, Anatolian 'grown-ups'; Finkelberg 1990/91: 80 n. 86 gives only the Luwian -mi ending.
VIR secures the human referent; *313a supplies an unknown qualification. RĀQIḪŪ 'perfumers' remains an unsupported contextual conjecture because the sign has no phonetic complement.
Ug. ṯġr 'gatekeeper', a personnel class (DULAT 888); gatekeepers of the house of God, Ezra 7:24. Rival: Akkadian tārû 'child-minder'.
23+22+24+13+5 = 87. Arithmetic establishes the summation function independently. Semitic *kull- 'all, entirety' is a possible etymological comparison; Linear B normally uses TO-SO for 'total.'
Cyperus, not cypress or copper. This begins the separate post-total commodity section. The value ¾ for A732 follows a modern fraction model and is not universally agreed.
AB30 functions logographically as FIC; NI is its syllabic value. The value ¼ for A704 is a defensible modern interpretation rather than an uncontested reading.
AB131a is the wine logogram; the final numeral is damaged.

HT89.translation: Captives of the sanctuary. Personnel classes: *305 23; A542 22; water(-men) 24; VIR+*313a 13; gatekeepers 5—total 87. Cyperus 2 + fraction; figs 2 + fraction; wine 6(?).
HT89.notes: HT89 is a personnel list followed by a separate commodity section. A-SA-RA₂ is one group on the tablet: /ʾasīr-/ 'captives' (Ug. åsr, DULAT 111; Akk. asīru, CAD A/2 331–32), SPECULATIVE; rival A + SA-RA₂ 'concerning the queen'. Uchitel includes *305, A542, MA-I-MI, VIR+*313a, and TA-RA among qualifications of personnel. Their counts sum exactly: 23+22+24+13+5 = KU-RO 87. Only after that total do A303/CYP, AB30/FIC, and AB131a/VIN appear. *307 is dubur 'sanctuary' (PK Za 8 = PK Za 15); MA-I-MI 'water(-men)' and TA-RA 'gatekeepers' are SPECULATIVE. The former expansions 'sacrificers,' 'offerings,' 'perfumers,' and 'turtledoves' are not treated as established. Fraction values ¾ and ¼ are model-dependent, and the final wine numeral is damaged.

words.gloss: final preserved sign of a lost word; not a standalone AROM logogram in this context
completion of yaššaram across a word-internal line break
and behold, may [...]; comparison with related formulae permits, but does not restore, a gathering clause

IOZa16.notes: Fragmentary libation table from the Iouktas peak sanctuary, MM III B–LM I. Diplomatic text: ] *123 · JA-SA-SA-RA- / -ME · U-NA-RU-KA[. The opening *123 is the final sign of a lost word; Karetsou, Godart, and Olivier (2002–2003, 445 n. 26) reject a standalone logographic reading in this context. The line break within JA-SA-SA-RA-ME is not a divider. At the other edge, only U-NA-RU-KA is preserved. Comparison with PK Za 11 and the U-NA-(RU)-KA-NA-SI/TI family permits a gathering clause as a bracketed reconstruction, but the editors explicitly decline to choose the lost ending (pp. 446–47). RU may represent Akkadian-style lū introducing a positive injunction in a verbless clause (Huehnergard 1997 §22.2), but its value remains uncertain (Duhoux 1992, 69–70; Thomas 2020, 2–3).

words.note: The inscription begins at a broken edge before NU. NU may be an asseverative particle (cf. Ug. n, Heb. nā, Akk. nū), but it may instead complete a lost word; it cannot be translated independently with confidence.

Possible b-preposition (cf. Heb. bə-, Ug. b-, Amarna bi-). A divider follows PA₃-E, while the Semitic preposition is normally proclitic, and the next group is presently read as a vocative. Its complement and exact syntax remain unresolved.

words.gloss: O Dikte, she of the Dubur
words.note: Name + TE (de) + *307-PU₂-RE dubur, the logogram with phonetic complement. The second TE stands only before dubur (PKZa8, PKZa15, PKZa11); the name alone has one dental (JA-DI-KI-TU, A-DI-KI-TE[, LB di-ka-ta-). TE = determinative de, cf. DU du; Ug. il d pid "El, the one of the heart" (KTU 1.4 IV 58–59). de CANDIDATE. Lit. "she of the Dubur": determinative + noun as a title, cf. Q 85:15 ذُو ٱلْعَرْشِ ḏū l-ʿarš "Owner of the Throne", Q 55:27 ذُو ٱلْجَلَٰلِ ḏū l-jalāl "Owner of Majesty", Nabataean ḏū-Šarā "Lord of the Shara."

Normalized TU-ME-I follows GORILA/Valério; Younger regards only TU as secure and questions whether the remaining traces form this group. ME is partial and I survives as three prong tops at the broken corner (GORILA IV 25). PK Za 14 ]-TU-ME-I · JA-SA-SA-[ secures the end of the group. If correct, Hebrew תֻּמִּי tummī 'my wholeness/integrity' (Ps 7:9; 26:1) supplies the exact nominal shape. 'Wholeness' preserves √t-m-m 'complete, without defect' while distinguishing it from the following √y-š-r 'uprightness/righteousness.' The imperative alternative 'be made whole!' is secondary.

Only JA-SA survives before a lacuna. Valério restores JA-SA-[SA-RA-ME] from the recurrent libation-formula word and prints a word divider before U-NA-KA-NA-SI; Younger's transcription likewise separates the two across the lacuna. The restored signs are not preserved, but the passage should not be encoded as the former continuous pseudo-word JA-SA-U-NA-KA-NA-SI.

Preserved after the lacuna following JA-SA. The semantic segmentation U-NA | KA-NA-SI is morphological, not marked by a written divider: conjunction + contracted presentative + 'my gathering.' The sequence is damaged again after SI.
Only I-PI survives at the broken end. Formulaic position supports restoration toward I-PI-[NA-MA] 'in the presence of,' but PKZa8 does not attest a complete standalone I-PI or the lost continuation.

PKZa8.translation: […] In/at […]—O Dikte, Mistress of the Dubur—my wholeness, [in righteousness]. So, behold my gathering in the pres[ence of …]
PKZa8.notes: Context: Fragmentary Palaikastro libation formula with DUBUR logogram and phonetic complement. Diplomatic sequence: ]NU · PA₃-E · JA-DI-KI-TE-TE-*307-PU₂-RE · TU-ME-I / JA-SA[ … ] U-NA-KA-NA-SI[ … ] / I-PI[ … ]. Valério 2007 restores JA-SA-[SA-RA-ME] | U-NA-KA-NA-SI; the former database form JA-SA-U-NA-KA-NA-SI incorrectly presented the two groups as one continuous word. JA-SA-[SA-RA-ME] and I-PI-[NA-MA] remain formulaic restorations, not preserved text. The translation leaves the opening and closing damage visible. TU-ME-I is rendered 'my wholeness' to distinguish √t-m-m completeness from √y-š-r righteousness while retaining their ritual pairing.

words.gloss: O Dikte, she of the Dubur (vocative yā + Diqqite + de + dubur)
words.note: Same phrase as PKZa8 with *307. The second TE stands only before dubur (PKZa8, PKZa15, PKZa11); the name alone has one dental (JA-DI-KI-TU, A-DI-KI-TE[, LB di-ka-ta-). TE = determinative de, cf. DU du; Ug. il d pid "El, the one of the heart" (KTU 1.4 IV 58–59). de CANDIDATE. Lit. "she of the Dubur": determinative + noun as a title, cf. Q 85:15 ذُو ٱلْعَرْشِ ḏū l-ʿarš "Owner of the Throne", Q 55:27 ذُو ٱلْجَلَٰلِ ḏū l-jalāl "Owner of Majesty", Nabataean ḏū-Šarā "Lord of the Shara."

PKZa15.translation: […] · O Dikte, Mistress of the Dubur […]
PKZa15.notes: Libation table rim (A.Nik. M.2469), left to right. GORILA IV 41: ] · JA-DI-KI-TE-TE-DU-PU₂-RE [ — a divider before JA, preceded by the trace of a sign (p.-ê. JA); broken after RE. Marked incomplete: text lost on both sides.

words.note: WA runs into the break; JA restored from the ten other witnesses.
Thomas 2020, 20 distinguishes only KA-NA, broken on both sides. Younger reads ]•-•-•SE-KA-NA-SI[•]TE[ and Hogan ∙ ∙ ∙ -ṢẸ-KA-NA-ṢI-[∙] ṬẸ-[, with SE, SI and TE uncertain and no divider. Not readable.
√š-y-r 'sing': abstract šīrūt in -ūt (Ugaritic syllabic ši-i-ru /šīru/ 'song'); not šērūt 'service' (√š-r-t).

SYZa3.translation: I make myself a dwelling […]-KA-NA-[…] sacred song.
SYZa3.notes: Context: Syme libation formula, fragmentary. Thomas 2020, 20 distinguishes only A-ṬẠ-Ị-*3̣0̣1-WA-[…]-KA-NA-[…] SI-RU-TE, with substantial text lost between the fragments (GORILA V 66–67, before the joins: ca. 20 signs). KA-NA stands in formula position 4, where the other sites have U-NA-KA-NA-SI.

words.gloss: O Šumāt! Olive (vocative + proper name + commodity ideogram)
words.note: Segment JA | SU-MA-TU: JA = Semitic vocative yā, paralleling JA-DI-KI-TU /yā Diktu/ in the same formula position. Birot, as reported by Huffmon (1965, p. 252), suggests that Amorite sumat- is a plural of sum- ‘name (> posterity),’ yielding *šum- + *-āt → Šumāt; TU carries a dead vowel after final /t/, and vowel length is unmarked. The corpus follows GORILA V 64–65 and Davis in reading the following sign as OLIV; Metaxa-Muhly 1984 and Finkelberg 1990 read it as syllabic RE, which may extend the name.

Beside OLE, compare √k-n-s for gathering produce as a cult offering: Neh 12:44 appoints men over the storerooms 'to gather into them' (לִכְנוֹס liḵnôs) the contributions, first fruits and tithes for the priests and Levites.

words.gloss: possible divine name or liturgical predicate; untranslated
words.note: A-JA is complete in GORILA V, 64–65. Mari writes West Semitic ḥaya "lives" as both ha-ia- and a-ia-, and Alalakh VII alternates a-ia-/ha-ia- in the same name; Weeden (2009, 96–100) suggests that a-ia- may reproduce an unrepresented /ḥ/. The Mesopotamian god Haya is independently written dḫa-ià and invoked in the Old Babylonian Hymn to Haia for Rim-Sin (ETCSL 2.6.9.2; line 59 links him with the petition "Give me life!"). Keep Haya, /ḥaya/ or /ḥayyā/ "(the) Living One/Life", and the goddess Aya as separate alternatives.

SYZa2.translation: I make myself a dwelling. O Šumāt! Olive, 1. So, behold my gathering: oil. [Haya?/the Living One?/Aya?]
SYZa2.notes: Context: Syme dialect libation formula with OLIV and OLE commodity ideograms. The sign immediately after SU-MA-TU is epigraphically disputed: GORILA V 64–65 and Davis read OLIV; Metaxa-Muhly 1984 and Finkelberg 1990 read RE. Final A-JA is complete, but its interpretation remains open: Haya, a √ḥ-y-y predicate or epithet, Aya, and Davis's "much" are rivals.

PKZa20.notes:
Context: Minimal fragment—only U-NA-KA preserved

One broken word, likely the beginning of the U-NA-KA-NA-SI formula.

words.note: Adjectival segmentation of undivided JA-SA-RA-A-NA-NE; a verbal jussive remains a rival.
GORILA IV 125 prints WI-PI-[·], one sign lost after PI. Not readable.

KNZc7.translation: This bowl, [for] release—O Athirat, [grant] righteous grace …
KNZc7.notes:
Context: ritual text painted inside a mended short conical cup; no numerals.

GORILA IV, 125 begins directly with complete A-KA-NU-ZA-TI and marks no opening lacuna, so there is no positive evidence for a lost word before A-KA-NU. Gordon segments that continuous group as A-KA-NU | ZA-TI. ZA-TI may be /zāt/ 'this' (historically perhaps /zāʾt/), with TI spelling final /t/ and a nonphonemic support vowel. Hebrew zō(ʾ)t supplies the lexical parallel. Phoenician ʾGN is feminine, and FK D 35 hʾgn hz 'this bowl' supplies the closest structural parallel (Krahmalkov 2000, 30). Its postposed Semitic order is rendered naturally in English as 'this bowl.' The former /ḏāti/ 'of' analysis is rejected because its final /i/ is a live genitive ending and the required agreement frame is absent. The segmentation remains CANDIDATE: ZA-TI is a hapax, SigLA reads ZE rather than ZA, and final TI = /t/ is not independently established. DU-RA-RE is glossed conservatively as 'freedom/release': compare Akkadian darāru and (an)durāru (CAD D, 109; CAD A/2, 115–17) and Hebrew dĕrōr (HALOT, 230). The supplied relation '[for] release' is interpretive because the syntax after 'this bowl' remains uncertain. A Nabataean inscription from Petra begins [d]nh ʾgnʾ dy qrb, 'This is the basin which ... offered,' and proceeds to the deity and bšlm šlm, 'in peace, peace' (CIS II 423b; Milik 1972, 109; Alpass 2013, 102 no. 16); it supports the vessel–deity–blessing frame but contains an explicit dedication verb. Safaitic f h lt s¹lm w h bʿls¹mn rwḥ, translated 'O Allāt [grant] security and O Baalshamin [grant] relief' (OCIANA AAEK 123 = ASFF 246), independently supports a verbless divine petition with editorial '[grant].' Athirat, not the bowl, is therefore the most defensible implied subject. The final group is WI-PI-[·] (GORILA IV, 125), one sign lost after PI. Not readable.

words.note: PS *dam-, Ugaritic dm /damu/; quantified like the neighboring allocation headings on HT95a/b and HT120. Rivals: dimtu 'district', Aramaic dəmē 'value of'.

HT95a.translation: Settlement(s)(?): grain. Blood (ritual category) 10, count/reckoning 10, king/royal establishment 20, emmer wheat 10, nobles/council(?) 10, parched grain(?) 7.
HT95a.notes: Context: Grain allocation—administrative tablet with GRA ideogram and commodity distributions. DA-ME is read damu 'blood', a recurring quantified ritual category; rivals dimtu 'district', Aramaic dmy 'value'. QE-RA₂-U /qelwu/ 'parched grain' is a second grain product beside KU-NI-SU 'emmer'.

words.note: √m-k-r 'to trade': Ugaritic mkrm 'merchants', counted in rosters with a total (DULAT 537); Akkadian mākiru, makkāru 'trader' (CAD M/1 129, 131). TE the -t of a class noun, cf. Akkadian tamkārūtu 'merchants (collective)' (CAD T 141). Rival: makritu 'red', of wool (CAD M/1 138).

devotee of Kubaba (personal name or title); rival Gupana

HT117a.translation: Merchants—owed: Ummī-naśiʾ: U-SU 1, Mītu 1, vineyard 1, MA-RU 1, Kubānu 1, TU-JU-MA 1, U-DI-MI 1, MI-RU-TA-RA-RE 1, bull 1, votive 1. Total: 10. SA-TA: KU-KU-DA-RA 1, KO-SA-I-TI 1, DA-MI-NU 1, DA-NE-KU-TI 1, Qidaru 1.
HT117a.notes:
Context: Personnel list—individual names with qty 1 allocations

MA-KA-RI-TE 'merchants' heads a roster of men owing 1 each, as Ugaritic lists count mkrm 'merchants' with a total (ġr mkrm, DULAT 537); rival makritu 'red' (CAD M/1 138). One written word in both witnesses. Personnel allocation list with named recipients. KI-RO is 'owed', not 'all, total'. U-MI-NA-SI heads the roster outside the count: the ten one-unit entries from U-SU to NA-DA-RE make KU-RO 10. KI-DA-RO is the personal name Qidaru, last of the SA-TA roster below the ruling. Six of the fifteen names recur as men's names in Linear B at Knossos: U-SU u-su (KN V 7512), TE-JA-RE te-ja-ro (KN V 479), NA-DA-RE no-da-ro (KN As 609), KU-KU-DA-RA ku-ka-da-ro (KN Uf 836), DA-MI-NU da-mi-ni-jo (KN D series), KI-DA-RO ki-da-ro (KN E 842); MA-RU compares with ma-ro at Pylos (PY Cn 328) (DMic I–II). Both sections list persons.

HT1.translation: Parched grain(?). Outstanding: 197. Zuzu(?) 70; DI-DI-ZA-KE 52; Kubānu 109; Aranare 105.
HT1.notes: Substantially intact LM IB administrative roster; no commodity logogram is present. KI-RO 197 is not a total: the four following quantities sum to 336. QE-RA₂-U /qelwu/ 'parched grain' heads the list, as it closes the HT95a/b grain set. ZU-SU compares with the Late Bronze Age Ugaritic personal name {m}zu-zu (RSO 7, 3, lower edge 3; ORACC P347841), though SU/ZU remains unexplained. DI-DI-ZA-KE has no secure external analysis. KU-PA₃-NU is Kubānu 'devotee of Kubaba', masculine of KU-PA₃-NA-TU Kubānatu (di Mino, Ya Diktu); the rival compares Ugaritic syllabic {m}gu-pa-na (RS 11.839 r.8; ORACC P503288), alphabetic Gupan, and Linear B ku-pa-nu-we-to. A-RA-NA-RE is strongly supported as a personal name by Linear B a-ra-na-ro (KN As 1516.11); Gordon's Egyptian 'Great-is-the-name-of-Re' remains a candidate etymology rather than the translation.

√q-l-w with RA₂=/la/: stands in the slot of QE-RA₂-U qelwu 'parched grain' in the HT95a/b set. Rival: Ugaritic qrwn 'offering' (DULAT 703; disputed as a PN).

HT86a.translation: Section 1—Agaru: emmer wheat, GRA+K+L: 20; king/royal establishment: 20; nobles/council(?): 20; parched grain: 10. Section 2—Addu: blood (ritual category), GRA+B: 20; count/reckoning: 20.

The preserved integer entries sum to 110; the GRA+K+L and GRA+B ligatures carry metrological riders and are not securely distinct grain species. DA-ME is read damu 'blood', a recurring quantified ritual category; rivals dimtu 'district' and Imperial Aramaic dmy nksyʾ 'the value of the property' (TAD B2.6 R.14), a later comparison. QA-RA₂-WA is read qalwa 'parched grain' (√q-l-w): it closes the HT95a/b set where QE-RA₂-U qelwu stands; rivals Ugaritic qrwn 'offering' and Linear B qa-ra₂-wo, a personal name. HT86b is an erased draft of the opening lines, not an independent witness.

It repeats HT86a lines 1–3 (A-KA-RU · KU-NI-SU GRA+K+L 20, SA-RU 20, DI-DE-RU 20) and is not an independent witness. DI-DE is the start of side a's DI-DE-RU; the erased text ends there.

HT88.translation: Work assignment/account(?): VIR+KA personnel 20; RE-ZA category or measure(?) 6; figs—Kikkina(?) 7. Outstanding: Kubaba 1, KA-JU 1, Kubānu 1, Payare 1, Samarō 1, DA-TA-RE 1. Total: 6.
HT88.notes: HT88 is substantially intact. KI-RO introduces exactly six one-unit labels and KU-RO 6 closes their sum; the lower section is therefore a secure outstanding/deficit roster, although not every label is demonstrably a personal name. A-DU is translated contextually as 'work assignment/account(?)' from Akkadian adū/addū; Addu/Haddu remains an alternative. VIR+KA is securely personnel, while kāribū is only a proposed expansion. RE-ZA is left as a category/measure. KI-KI-NA is Kikkina, supported by Amorite KIKKIN names; the former Ugaritic 'pot' comparison incorrectly omitted final -t. KU-PA₃-NU is a probable personal name or title, compared with Ugaritic gu-pa-na/gpn and Linear B ku-pa-nu-we-to; Kubānu 'devotee/priest of Kubaba' remains an alternative project hypothesis, not an attested title. Payare is supported as a Minoan name by Linear B pa-ja-ro, not translated as Egyptian 'He-of-Re.' Samarō remains a name with NWS and Egyptian comparisons. KA-JU and DA-TA-RE remain unread.

if separate, possibly ‘in/by’ or administrative shorthand ‘in the charge of’
probable Hurrian-style personal name; cf. Ugaritic Taki-šenni
commodity ideogram; possibly a Pistacia/terebinth product

HT103.translation: Uta/Uda(?)—figs 40; under/in the charge of(?) Takušenni(?) 6½; commodity *188, possibly a Pistacia/terebinth product, 13; Daguna 1; Takušenni(?) 1; orchard/garden(?) 5½.
HT103.notes: Administrative list; the relations among most entries are not grammatically expressed. GORILA I 170–171 allows a possible divider after PA₃, so PA₃ may be a separate abbreviation or part of PA₃-DA-KU-SE-NE. If separate, PA₃ before a probable personal name and quantity closely parallels Ugaritic/Phoenician bd /bādi/ or /bīdi/ ‘in the charge of’: Kition no. 84 repeats bd + personal name + a count of workmen. Ugaritic CAT 4.145:9–10 similarly has bd rb hršm ‘in the custody of the chief of the craftsmen’; Akkadian writes ša qāti ‘in the charge of’ with NĪG.ŠU before personal names. PA₃ could thus represent b- ‘in/by’ or a local administrative shorthand for bād(i). The latter is not an established Semitic abbreviation, however, and the standard Linear B coda rule does not license omission of final /d/. Linear B pa-ro + personal name ‘in whose care/in the charge of’ is a functional Aegean parallel. The first DA-KU-SE-NE is damaged in two sign positions in SigLA. NI securely denotes figs: AB30 depicts a fig branch and functions as the Aegean fig ideogram (Montecchi 2024, 178, following Neumann 1957, 157–58). TE-*301 occurs only on HT8a and HT98a and may spell Semitic /tēnā/ ‘fig,’ but that candidate does not establish NI’s meaning. NI 40 is not marked as a total and no KU-RO occurs. U-TA₂ probably labels an entity or place; Uta/Uda is a comparison, not an identification. Exact Dakušenni is not attested at Nuzi: /Takušenni/ is a cautious reconstruction from Nuzi Aku-šenni, Takku, and Takuja and Ugaritic Taki-šenni; only Hurrian -šenni ‘brother’ is secure as an onomastic comparison. DA-KU-NA matches attested Daguna and is safest here as a personal name, probably Dagan/Dagon-derived. The commodity status of *188 is secure, while the Pistacia identification remains probable. KI-RA is tentatively compared with Akkadian kirû ‘garden, orchard,’ which fits HT103 and its heading position before a fig entry on ZA8; Akkadian qīru ‘liquid bitumen’ is a formally close but contextually weaker alternative. Neither is established.

hapax transaction sign; exact operation unknown
probable Hurrian-style name or entity with final TI: 45½
words.note: Bare DA-KU-SE-NE occurs on HT 103 .4–5; on .2–3 a break follows NE. The comparison with Ugaritic Taki-šenni supports the name analysis, but the exact form and the function of TI remain uncertain.
On the Eblaite name element yidu 'strength' (Pagan 1998); TI is unexplained. Rivals: I-DU followed by TI as an ideogram; Ida, written I-DA-A at KOZa1.
No verified Luwian or Semitic match. The alleged bare PA-DA-SU parallel on HT20 depends on an obsolete reading; the current transcription is PA-RO-SU.

HT104.notes: Inter-entity transfer list with an unspecified commodity and unresolved direction. The arithmetic is exact: 45½ + 20½ + 29 = 95. Repeated final TI defines a shared administrative or morphological class. The DA-KU-SE-NE / DA-KU-SE-NE-TI pair favors suffixation, while GORILA I 171 allows TI to be an ideogram or classifier. Finkelberg (2002/03, 96–97) proposes a dative/recipient interpretation, ‘for/to’; HT104 does not establish an ablative ‘from.’

words.note: The inscription begins at a broken edge. TA is the preserved end of a word, not an independently attested particle.

widd 'love' + ti(h)āmu 'the Deep' (Ug. thm, DULAT 851; Heb. təhôm), as Ug. ydd il 'beloved of El'. Sign dispute: GORILA IV 161 reads WI and MU, both doubtful; a second reading takes the fourth sign as RU.
Feminine participle of √w-q-d 'to burn', as Heb. yōqedet (Isa 65:5), with w- written by U as in U-NA-KA-NA-SI. A divider separates it from WI-TE-JA-MU (GORILA IV 161).

JA-SA-SA-RA is preserved, followed only by a damaged vertical trace. ME is the conventional formulaic restoration; NE cannot be excluded. The established formulaic lexeme permits the tentative contextual gloss, but PL Zf 1 does not independently preserve its ending.

Proposed internal segmentation TA-NU-NI / KI-NA: expected Hebrew 2fs Piʿel imperative /tannî/ from √t-n-y ‘recount, recite’ (Judg 5:11; 11:40) plus qînâ ‘funeral song, dirge’ (HALOT, 1097, 1759–60). HALOT's proposed antiphonal repetition motivates the natural translation ‘chant a dirge’; the stricter lexical gloss is ‘recite/repeat.’ The funerary context suits the phrase, but the inscription writes no divider between the two proposed words.

Its position after the proposed imperative-object phrase favors a noun, contextually a vocative. Hebrew nîn means ‘offspring, descendants.’ NI-NU-NI can spell /nīn-ūn/ exactly if final I is dead; alternatively /nīn-un/ would contain Arabic-type nominative nunation. Both are grammatically regular Semitic analyses: -ūn may represent plural or collective morphology, while -un is an indefinite nominative ending. What remains uncertain is which ending the Linear A spelling encodes and whether the noun functions as a vocative here. Since this exact inflected form is unattested for nîn and NI-NU-NI is a hapax, the identification remains speculative. CAD N/2 supplies no Akkadian ninû ‘offspring.’
One lost sign flanks I on each side (GORILA IV 161, which allows [·]-I-MA); it is not a standalone word or suffixal attestation.

PLZf1.translation: […] Beloved of the Deep(?), the Burning One(?), in righteousness(?)—Chant a dirge, O offspring. […]
PLZf1.coverage: Every group but the broken ]TA and [?]-I-[?] receives a tentative gloss
PLZf1.notes: PL Zf 1 is a fragmentary LM I inscription on a silver pin from the immediate vicinity of Platanos Tholos A, a funerary rather than peak-sanctuary context (Monti 2022, 113). It is read sinistroverse. Initial ]TA and final [?]-I-[?] are word fragments, WI and MU in WI-TE-JA-MU are doubtful, and the ending of JA-SA-SA-RA-[ME?] is restored. The final preserved phrase is now provisionally read /tannî qînâ nīnūn/, ‘Chant a dirge, O offspring.’ The lack of a divider within TA-NU-NI-KI-NA and the ambiguity between grammatically regular plural/collective -ūn and case -un keep the identifications speculative; the morphology itself is well formed. ‘Posterity’ remains a possible interpretive gloss for /nīnūn/, not the direct translation. Duhoux's structural analysis makes WI-TE-JA-MU and U-QE-TI possible onomastic X-terms, but this is a syntactic classification, not a decipherment.

Duhoux 1992, 80–81: supplementary X-terms as possible personal names
Monti 2022, 113: funerary context; not a votive offering

IOZa9.support: Surviving corner of a square marble libation table (HM 3898)

words.note: Proposed adverbial accusative /yaššaram/ from √y-š-r; -am is represented by final ME. The divine-name reading Yasharam remains an alternative but is not required here. On IO Za 9 only ]JA-SA-SA- survives; GORILA restores RA-ME (V 33).

U-NA is provisionally /wannā/ 'and behold,' or, more naturally here, 'so, behold,' comparing Ugaritic w hn beside contracted wn and Lipiński's *wa-hanna/u; the vowels remain reconstructed. KA-NA-SI = kanāsī 'my gathering' (G verbal noun of √k-n-s + 1cs -ī); Aramaic-shaped alternative knāšī; Syriac knšy 'gather!' (Peshitta Jer 10:17) is a verbal rival. On IO Za 9 only U̇-NA-KA-[ survives; GORILA restores NA-SI (V 33).

IOZa9.notes: IO Za 9 is preserved on the broken corner of a square marble libation table. Line a is retrograde and line b runs in the opposite direction, so both read outward from the corner (GORILA V, 32–33; Younger 2023, citing Palaima 1988, 310–12). Line a keeps ]JA-SA-SA- and line b U̇-NA-KA-[; GORILA and Younger restore RA-ME and NA-SI from the formula. Both words are read in full elsewhere: JA-SA-SA-RA-ME on IO Za 6 and PS Za 2, U-NA-KA-NA-SI on KO Za 1, PK Za 8, SY Za 2 and TL Za 1. PK Za 27 breaks after U-NA-KA- too.

words.note: Preserved after a broken left edge: ]I-PI-NA-MA. The p-n 'face/front' family supports the contextual sense 'in the presence of'; -MA may be an enclitic =ma.

TE is read beyond a damaged join after RU: SI-RU[-TE. The normalized form is secured by intact formulaic parallels. √š-y-r 'sing': possible abstract šīrūt in -ūt; Ugaritic syllabic ši-i-ru /šīru/ 'song'.

IOZa15.translation: […] in the presence of sacred song.
IOZa15.notes: Damaged witness of positions 5–6 of the IO Za 2 formula: ]I-PI-NA-MA · SI-RU[-TE. The preceding text is lost, and TE is read beyond a damaged join after RU. The normalized pair is supported by intact IO Za 2 and KO Za 1. I-PI-NA-MA is interpreted contextually as 'in the presence of'; 'sacred song' renders the proposed abstract šīrūt from √š-y-r, not 'service/ministry' from √š-r-t.

words.note: The complete first group permits the adverbial accusative *yaššaram*, 'in righteousness.' Yasharam as a divine name remains a secondary possibility.

Only Ụ-NA-KA- is reasonably preserved; the following trace may belong to NA, while final SI is lost. The editors prefer AB10 U over AB45 DE from the outline and formulaic context. Restoration as U-NA-KA-[NA-SI] follows the recurrent formula, so both kanāsī and its 1cs suffix remain restored here.

PKZa27.notes: The Neopalatial Petsophas fragment preserves complete JA-SA-SA-RA-ME after a divider, followed by Ụ-NA-KA-[ or possibly Ụ-NA-KA-ṆẠ[ before the break (Knappett, Del Freo, and Zurbach 2017, 73–80). It belongs to the same abbreviated formulaic pair as IO Za 9 but is not an independently complete duplicate. No preserved element means 'holy.'

words.note: The vessel is broken before TE. This is the end of a lost word, not an independently attested TE particle; [SI-RU]-TE is a possible restoration but is not epigraphically recoverable.

I-DA is the inscription's only complete group: it is bounded by dividers despite the breaks on both outer edges. The proposed identification is Mount Ida (Psiloritis), the sacred mountain of central Crete.

The second JA reaches the broken right edge; no divider or word ending survives. The preserved beginning may continue a form of Semitic √ḥ-y-y 'live; life,' allowing the contextual restoration '[the Living One …],' but JA-JA is not a complete word and cannot independently establish /ḥayyā/.

PKZa18.coverage: 1/1 complete word translated; 2 edge fragments untranslated
PKZa18.notes: Context: broken stone-vessel inscription from Palaikastro. Diplomatic text: ]-TE · I-DA · JA-JA-[…. Both outer groups run into breaks; I-DA alone is complete between dividers. 'Ida, [the Living One …]' is a contextual restoration, not a word-for-word decipherment of the damaged groups.

words.note: CONFIRMED libation formula opener. 11 attestations across 5 peak sanctuary sites. Gt-stem imperfective of √NWY.

JA-JA is followed immediately by the broken right edge, so the word's length and ending are unknown. The shared beginning with PKZa18 is structurally noteworthy, and √ḥ-y-y 'live; life' remains a candidate comparison, but the fragment cannot establish /ḥayyā/ or a complete epithet.

SYZa8.coverage: 1/1 complete word translated; trailing fragment untranslated
SYZa8.notes: Context: Peak-sanctuary libation vessel (LMIA). The formula opener is followed by JA-JA-[…] at the broken right edge. Compare PKZa18, where the same preserved beginning also runs into a break; neither witness preserves a complete JA-JA word.

words.note: First sign: the foot of an upright only (DA, A, ME or SA). Fourth sign: perhaps ZU over WA over JA. Broken after SE (Muhly and Olivier 2008, 211). Not readable.

SYZb7.notes: Fragment of a terracotta zoomorphic rhyton (?) from the Syme sanctuary (Muhly and Olivier 2008, 210–11, fig. 9). Six positions, broken after the sixth. The four-sign RA-KI-NI-SE omits the fourth sign and does not support la-kinnisēt.

words.note: The signs are preserved after a broken left edge, so the inscription itself does not preserve the group's opening boundary. The recurrent formula supports segmentation as I-PI-NA-MA; the p-n 'face/front' family supports the contextual sense 'in the presence of,' and -MA may be an enclitic =ma.

A following divider secures the right boundary. 'Sacred song' renders the proposed abstract šīrūt in -ūt from √š-y-r 'sing' (Ugaritic syllabic ši-i-ru /šīru/ 'song'); it is not a separately written adjective and not šērūt 'service' (√š-r-t).

VRYZa1.translation: […] in the presence of sacred song […]
VRYZa1.notes: Fragmentary witness of positions 5–6 of the IO Za 2 formula on a square serpentine libation table. The text is written retrograde. The surface is broken before I-PI-NA-MA, while a divider follows SI-RU-TE and the continuation is lost. The normalized pair is secured by intact formulaic parallels, including IO Za 2 and KO Za 1. 'Sacred song' is the English rendering adopted for the proposed abstract noun šīrūt.

words.gloss: Storm God (= Hadad/Baal)—heading/recipient; rival adû 'work assignment'

words.note: PS *dam-, Ugaritic dm /damu/; quantified like the neighboring allocation headings on HT95a/b and HT120. Rivals: dimtu 'district', Aramaic dəmē 'value of'.

HT95b.translation: For Addu: king/royal establishment 10, [break], blood (ritual category) 10, count/reckoning 10, emmer wheat 10, nobles/council(?) 10, parched grain(?) 10.
HT95b.notes:
Context: Allocation ledger for the Storm God Addu—same six category words as recto (HT95a) with adjusted quantities, all standardized to 10 units except possible lost entry at break

Verso of HT95a. Same six allocation categories as recto but with different quantities—recto has SA-RU 20 and QE-RA₂-U 7; verso standardizes all to 10. The recto header DA-DU-MA-TA · GRA names the institution and commodity (grain); the verso header A-DU names the divine recipient (Storm God). Together the two sides likely represent two related distributions: one institutional (recto), one cultic (verso). The fragment markers between SA-RU and DA-ME indicate at least one lost entry. All six categories match exactly between recto and verso—the same allocation vocabulary in a different fiscal context.

words.note: Compound: SU-PU₂ /sapu/ "jar" + *188 BUṬNU "terebinth" logogram. Commodity heading.
PA₃ = /ba/ confirms the initial syllable of BUṬNU, paralleling *307-PU₂-RE pattern for DUBUR.

√q-y-n. Arabic qayn 'smith, artisan'; Sabaic qyn 'administrator, governor' (Biella 1982, 454). Also appears on HT8a recto (¾ unit)—the same recurring recipient label in both oil and terebinth registers.
√k-p-r. Here likely a recipient designation—"(for) the village."

words.gloss: He (of) Re: Egyptian personal name Pꜣ-Rꜥ (PNM v6)
words.note: Egyptian-derived PN. Receiving 1⅛ units of terebinth product.
*86 (PROBABLE /na/) compounded with *188 BUṬNU. May indicate a specific grade or preparation of terebinth product. Receiving ½ unit.

HT8b.translation: Bowl of terebinth (pistachio) nuts: 1. [divider] 5. Terebinth: 2. Qaynī (smith or administrator): 1⅜. Village: ½. Payare: 1⅛. [*86]-terebinth: ½. [½].
HT8b.notes:
Context: Terebinth product accounting—commodity ledger with fractional quantities (⅜, ⅛, ½), tracking resin/mastic distributions to named recipients

Verso of HT8a. The recto records olive oil (OLE+KI) distributions; the verso records terebinth (*188) product distributions. QA-*310-I appears on both sides—the same recipient drawing from two commodity registers. Fractional quantities (⅜, ⅛, ½) suggest measurement of liquid or semi-liquid products (resin, oil). The phonetic complement PA₃-*188 confirms the /b/-onset reading of *188 as BUṬNU, paralleling the DUBUR pattern (*307-PU₂-RE). Five of six substantive words are in the lexicon (83%).

words.note: Gt-stem imperfective 1cs of √NWY. Same formula-initial position as IOZa2.
Single sign AU followed by break. Possibly ideogram for 'pig' (SUS) per GORILA, or beginning of next formula word.

IOZa3.notes:
Context: Peak sanctuary libation formula—fragmentary (formula verb + damaged ending)

Fragmentary. Only the formula verb survives intact. The AU sign at the break may be ideographic (commodity) rather than part of the prayer.

words.note: Gt-stem imperfective 1cs of √NWY. Same formula-initial position.

words.gloss: broken word after the formula verb; *321 has no value
words.note: Broken after *321 (GORILA V 28–29).

IOZa7.translation: I make myself a dwelling · JA-TI-*321[…]
IOZa7.notes: Libation table, left end intact, broken after *321 (GORILA V 28–29). The divider is cut over an erased JA.

words.note: Gt-stem imperfective 1cs of √NWY. Syme attestation confirms inter-site formula distribution.

I-DA = Mount Ida (I-DA-A, KO Za 1; I-DA-[, IO Za 2) + mī 'waters' (√m-y-y; Hebrew mayim, Ugaritic my); or -mī 1cs, 'my Ida'. Position 2 names the sanctuary's mountain, as JA-DI-KI-TU at Iouktas. Rival: personal name ʾIdāmī (√ʾ-d-m).
Single sign JA at break. Possibly beginning of next formula word (JA-SA-SA-RA-ME or JA-DI-KI-TU).

SYZa1.translation: I make myself a dwelling—Waters of Ida… [broken]
SYZa1.notes:
Context: Peak sanctuary libation formula—Syme variant

MMIIIB date makes this among the earliest formula attestations. I-DA-MI in position 2 names Mount Ida, as JA-DI-KI-TU names Dikte at Iouktas and I-DA-A Ida at Kophinas; a personal name is the rival. The trailing JA- at the break hints at a continuation into the standard formula sequence.

words.note: tG-stem 1cs of √n-w-y; same reading as the other ten copies and the lexicon entry. LMIA date.

Position 2, the divine address. Vocative ya + ʾanwaru, elative of √n-w-r 'light'; I- writes the aleph. RILA-S1 p. 84 reads JA-I-NWA-RO with RO underdotted; GORILA's ZA is 'moins probable'. Sign 3 is NWA (AB48), its only occurrence in the corpus. Rival: ʾaṣwaru 'Fashioner' if AB48 wrote a sibilant + w.
Position 3. √b-n-y 'to build' — active participle with nisbe. Divine craftsman epithet (cf. Ugaritic Kothar-wa-Khasis). RILA-S1 underdots WI; PA₃-NI-PI is less plausible.

SYZa4.translation: I make myself a dwelling, O Radiant One, the Builder
SYZa4.notes:
Context: Peak sanctuary libation formula—Syme variant with unique second and third words

LMIA Syme peak sanctuary. Word 1 is the tG-stem formula verb (CONFIRMED). Word 2 = yā ʾanwaru 'O Radiant One' (SPECULATIVE; RILA-S1 p. 84). Word 3 = bānīy 'the Builder' (CANDIDATE). The epithet pair matches Ugaritic El's ṯr il dpid // bny bnwt 'Builder of Built (Ones)' (KTU 1.4 III 30–32).

words.gloss: may you (f.) be gracious (if TA begins the word)
words.note: Conditional G u-class analysis of √n-ʿ-m. Arabic naʿuma/yanʿumu supports the u-vocalism, and Sabaic n²m ‘be favourable, prosper’ supplies the closest semantics (Beeston et al. 1982, 90). TA is the Semitic t-prefix; TI is di Mino's proposed analogical 2fs subject clitic. The initial break, unwritten ʿ, and unattested prefix verb + -tī combination keep the reading tentative; Thomas's TI-as-plural analysis remains a rival.

One graphic word across the side break. Amorite IA-SA-RA-AM directly attests accusative /yašaram/ (Gelb 1980, no. 3448), supporting an adverbial accusative ‘uprightly.’ Final NA is provisionally emphatic/topical =na, compared with Ugaritic -n or -(Vn)na (Tropper §§89.1–2); no exact /yašaram=na/ is attested. Ordinary Semitic dual and plural endings do not yield -MA-NA, so the former ‘righteous portion/Righteous Allotter’ analysis is withdrawn.
GORILA IV 9 prints DA-WA-[·]-ḌU-WA-ṬO, one sign lost inside the word. Not readable.
Right-broken. The preserved signs may begin the Semitic ‘island’ word, but the incomplete form cannot support the former translation ‘of the island.’

KNZa10.translation: […] May you indeed be gracious and upright …
KNZa10.notes: GORILA IV, 8–9 gives ]TA-NU-MU-TI · JA-SA-SA-RA-MA / NA · DA-WA-[·]-ḌU-WA-ṬO · I-JA[. No divider separates MA from NA, so JA-SA-SA-RA-MA-NA is one graphic word across the side break. If the initial TA begins a word, the proposed strict rendering is ‘may you be gracious—in righteousness indeed’; the smoother translation below renders the adverbial phrase as coordinated English. The lexical controls are √n-ʿ-m ‘be gracious/favourable’ and Amorite /yašaram/ ‘uprightly’; the 2fs -tī and emphatic =na remain analogical proposals. The two final groups are damaged and left untranslated.

words.note: N-stem √ʿ-n-y in the TA-NA-[X]-U-TI-NU frame of IO Za 2 word 7: 2fs prefix + subject clitic -tī + 1cp object -n. The 2fs verb addresses the following theonym I-NA-TA-I (ʿInatī, "my Anat").

Theonym plus 1cs -ī. Initial I is tentatively laryngeal-bearing rather than a separate particle. Ugaritic has three vowel-conditioned aleph signs (Huehnergard 2012, 21), while syllabic Ugaritic writes ᵈa-na-tu₄ for /ʿanatu/ and ša-i for /šāʿi/ (Huehnergard 2008, 18 n. 78, 208, 249). These are orthographic parallels, not proof of the Linear A value.

words.gloss: Breast (first member of a divine epithet)
words.note: First member of the proposed compound epithet ṯudī-šiqā, 'Breast-Who-Gives-Drink'; compare Ugaritic ṯd in KTU 1.23 b-ṯd aṯrt, 'at the breast of Athirat.'

words.gloss: Who Gives Drink (second member of a divine epithet)
words.note: Second member of ṯudī-šiqā; compare Ugaritic šqy, Hebrew hišqā, and Akkadian šaqû, 'give drink.' The deity-plus-epithet construction is structurally comparable with Ugaritic btlt ʿnt, 'the young woman Anat' (KTU 1.3 III 11).
Adverbial accusative. Polysemic layer: masculine divine name Yasharam (Akk. Mīšarum, Phoen. Misor).

IOZa6.translation: May you (f.) answer us, my Anat, Breast-Who-Gives-Drink, in righteousness.
IOZa6.notes: The stone vessel is chipped, but the written sequence is complete: all three groups and their dividers survive, with no lacuna inside I-NA-TA-I-ZU-DI-SI-KA. The middle group is tentatively segmented I-NA-TA-I + ZU-DI + SI-KA, a theonym followed by a compound epithet. Ugaritic supplies the orthographic controls: three vowel-conditioned aleph signs (Huehnergard 2012, 21), syllabic ᵈa-na-tu₄ = /ʿanatu/, and ša-i = /šāʿi/ (Huehnergard 2008, 18 n. 78, 208, 249). Together these permit—but do not prove—a laryngeal-bearing initial I; final I is read as 1cs -ī. Ugaritic btlt ʿnt 'the young woman Anat' (KTU 1.3 III 11) and Middle Babylonian Ištar-ṣēri provide deity-plus-epithet controls. The rival segmentation with bare I-NA as a presentative remains possible but is less economical in this complete 2fs-verb + addressee context.

words.note: The vessel is broken immediately before NA. A divider survives after SI, but no initial boundary is preserved. KH7a has the distinct form E-NA-SI and is not an independent attestation of NA-SI.
The comparison with Semitic pnm 'face, presence' is PROBABLE from five complete occurrences elsewhere. This APZa2 occurrence ends at a break without a divider and is capped at CANDIDATE.

words.gloss: a form of KU-PA₃-NA-TU, its ending lost. Not readable.
words.note: GORILA IV 5 prints ]-KU-PA₃-NA-TU-NA-TE[, with a trace before KU, perhaps I. Neither exterior boundary nor any internal divider is preserved.

A divider survives after TE, but the beginning is lost; PI and MI over an erasure (GORILA IV 5). PI cannot securely be isolated as a preposition. Ugaritic mnt 'part, portion' and Semitic √m-n-y remain comparisons only. Rival: Heb. minḥâ 'offering', Ug. mnḥt 'tribute'.
No divider follows TA. Roughly three sign spaces are lost before final -QA, so the sequence may continue through the lacuna. The Semitic segmentation remains only a candidate.
Only final QA and the following divider survive; no root or syntactic function can be recovered.

APZa2.notes: Fragmentary two-line inscription on two nonjoining pieces of one serpentine jar (HM 2479 + HM 2480). Every preserved sequence is edge-damaged. I-PI-NA-MA has substantial independent lexical support. The longer sequence, ]-KU-PA₃-NA-TU-NA-TE[ with a trace before KU (perhaps I), contains the independently attested Kupanatu base and additional morphology. The fragments do not permit reconstruction of a continuous sentence. Younger estimates six lost sign spaces in the first internal lacuna and three in the second; these are not readable signs.

words.gloss: bowl or vessel; perhaps a vessel-account heading
words.note: Compare Akkadian diqāru and Late Bronze Age Ugaritic /dikāru/ 'bowl' (alphabetic plural dkrt). Huehnergard treats the Ugaritic item as an Akkadian or shared early loan, not necessarily an inherited root. DA-QE-RA occurs on HT6a, HT57a and HT120; its written vowels do not exactly match /dikāru/.
PS *dam-, Ugaritic dm /damu/; quantified like the neighboring allocation headings on HT95a/b and HT120. Rivals: dimtu 'district', Aramaic dəmē 'value of'.

Read /Dawmi/, from √d-w-m 'endure, remain,' with U representing medial /w/ and *49 carrying /mi/. The sign may be syllabic here while functioning logographically or as an abbreviated commodity sign elsewhere; such polyvalence removes any contradiction with PALM/TREE or its candidate lexical name TAMIR.
SigLA catalogues this as the single composite logogram A517; do not segment it as I + GRA+PA without further evidence.
GORILA groups line-final KI with line-initial RE-TA-NA; the complete form is independently attested on HT2, HT8a and HT108.

HT120.translation: DA-QE-RA account(?), perhaps concerning a vessel or measure. Blood (ritual category): grain category K+L 74 and grain category PA 62½. Dawmi: A517 20. Kretana—the Cretan or Crete: grain category B 60 and grain category PA 48. Phaistos: 3⅕.
HT120.notes: Administrative grain account arranged under parallel entity or category headings. DA-ME is read damu 'blood', a ritual category heading grain allocations; its quantified use on HT95a/b and HT120 weighs against the later Aramaic dəmē 'value of', and dimtu 'district' is the other rival. DA-QE-RA has Akkadian and Ugaritic /dikāru/ 'bowl' as a Bronze Age comparison, although the written vowels differ. DA-U-*49 is read Dawmi, with *49=/mi/ here; possible logographic use of *49 elsewhere does not exclude that syllabic value. GORILA groups cross-line KI-RE-TA-NA, independently confirmed by three complete attestations. PA-I-TO securely names Phaistos. The tablet does not itself express direction, shipment or taxation.

words.note: Heads a mixed commodity section here and on HT 131a. If *118 = ṭa, cf. Arabic iqṭaʿ 'cut, divide' (√q-ṭ-ʿ); *118 = ṭa is speculative. Rivals: a personal or institutional name.
quantity lost at the tablet’s right edge
quantity lost (break)

HT44a.translation: I-QA-*118 (heading): grain [quantity lost]; KI oil 3; U oil 5; RA oil 5; olives 1; figs 1; wine [quantity lost].
HT44a.notes: Context: mixed commodity inventory under a repeated administrative heading. I-QA-*118 also heads a commodity section on HT131a. If *118 = ṬA, Arabic iqṭaʿ ‘cut, divide’ provides a formal and semantically relevant comparison, but no direct Bronze Age administrative use of the form is established; a personal or institutional name remains possible. OLE+KI and OLE+U have candidate interpretations elsewhere in the lexicon, whereas OLE+RA is unique and remains unidentified. The photograph confirms right-edge damage after GRA and VIN.

words.gloss: field or estate heading; possibly the deified Ugaritic 'Field'

HT2.translation: A-KA-RU—farm or estate account(?): U-oil 20[…], A-oil 17, E-oil 3[…]. […] KI-RE-TA-NA—Kretana/Cretan(?): U-oil 54[…]. […] A-oil 47. Isolated tally: 1.
HT2.notes: GORILA I, p. 5 shows right-edge losses after 20, 3, and 54, and left-edge damage before KI-RE-TA-NA and OLE+A 47. The preserved oil numerals total at least 141. The isolated 1 follows a blank line and lacks a commodity sign; it is not an oil fraction or secure section subtotal. A-KA-RU probably denotes a farm or estate account: Ugaritic ugr and Akkadian ugāru support 'field,' while Akkadian ikkaru 'farmer; farm bailiff,' Hebrew ʾikkār, and Aramaic ʾakkārā supply an administrative rival. KI-RE-TA-NA remains plausibly 'Kretana/Cretan,' but its precise function and any export interpretation are unproved.

words.note: GORILA III 11 .1 ]-JA-PI GRA 6[, broken before, the traces perhaps *306 (note). Not readable.
GORILA III 11 .2 ]PI-*314̣ GRA 1[, broken before, PI over an erasure, *314 dotted. Not readable.

ARKH3b.notes: Commodity list, broken at the left on every line (GORILA III 11). Both syllabic groups are the ends of lost words.

words.gloss: initial administrative heading; possibly an entity, place, transaction, or Addu/Haddu

words.note: quantity lost (break)

HT99a.translation: A-DU [heading]. SA-RA₂ [recipient or institution]: cyperus 4[...]; figs 4[...]; wine 1 + A706 (≈⅙?); flour/meal(?) [...].
HT99a.notes: A-DU is an initial administrative heading, but its distribution does not establish Addu/Haddu over an entity, place, or transactional interpretation. SA-RA₂ is better treated as a recipient or institutional heading than as 'surplus'; 'queen/princess' or 'royal establishment' is the leading Semitic candidate. CYP is the cyperus logogram, not copper. Damage follows CYP 4 and NI 4; A706 is conventionally valued at approximately ⅙, and the final GRA+QE quantity is lost.

words.gloss: unidentified counted category; quantity lost, 4 inferred from KU-RO 97

words.note: Including KI 2 and reconstructing 4 after *304+PA yields 58+4+12+2+5+16=97. Montecchi's alternative restores 6 and excludes KI by expanding it to KI-RO, but RO is not written.

Hebrew cult inventories repeatedly use šemen ham-mišḥā 'the anointing oil' (Exod 25:6; 29:7; 31:11), and Ugaritic attests mšḥ 'anoint' (DUL 585). Akkadian pašāšum with šamnum is a semantic parallel only (Huehnergard 1997, §5.5).

HT100.translation: Personnel or accounting categories: VIR+KA 58, *304+PA [4 inferred], TI+A 12, KI 2, *305 5, VIR+*313a 16. Total: 97. For the queen/royal establishment: cyperus 5¼, figs 2⅓, wine 2½, oil (U) 2 + A706, anointing oil(?) 3, oil (NE) ¾.
HT100.notes: Context: personnel register followed by a separate commodity allocation. The quantity after *304+PA is lost; including every preserved category requires 4, since 58+4+12+2+5+16=97. Montecchi's alternative restores 6 and excludes KI 2 by expanding KI to KI-RO, but RO is not written. *305 is securely a personnel category, but its exact class is unknown. SA-RA₂ is a recipient or institutional heading; 'queen/princess' or 'royal establishment' remains CANDIDATE. OLE+MI is tentatively 'anointing oil': Hebrew šemen ham-mišḥā supplies the exact commodity expression, and Ugaritic mšḥ supports the root. CYP denotes cyperus. *304's former syllabic reading remains suspended.

words.note: Heads the first mixed-commodity allocation. Judson (2017, 88 nn. 237–239) regards *22F here as a probable but uncertain syllabographic use. The unresolved medial sign prevents a responsible lexical reading.
The project comparison with Semitic *qamāḥ- and qemāḥ/qēmu 'flour, meal' remains a candidate; the tablet itself establishes only a grain subtype.
The adjuncts distinguish oil categories; their proposed lexical expansions are not required for the account's structure.

Occupies the same structural position as ZU-*22F-DI and KU-PA₃-[…]. HT101 therefore supports an entity, recipient, institution, place, or title rather than 'surplus'; the positive royal identification remains a comparative hypothesis.
Its independent occurrence with a quantity establishes a commodity compound, but not the proposed identification as a honey product.
A lacuna follows PA₃ before OLE+U 2. Comparison with seven complete KU-PA₃-NU attestations makes [NU] the strongest internal restoration, but it is not preserved and is not counted as an attestation.
The horizontal rule begins a separate account; the commodity preceding 20 is lost.
Its status as a quantified commodity is secure. Identification with Semitic *pidr- 'fat, tallow' remains tentative.
Damage extends across the end of line 5 and beginning of line 6; the two quantities must not be silently joined or assigned to the same commodity.
*OLIV+TU is a distinct and uncommon olive subtype. Its precise sense, including the proposed comparison with wild olives, is unproved.

HT101.translation: ZU-*22F-DI: grain-QE 40; oil-U 8, oil-MI 8, oil-KI 2. The queen/royal establishment(?): grain 41, oil 10, DI+QE 3. KU-PA₃-[…]: oil-U 2. — [Damaged commodity] 20; *304 3; oil-KI 2[; ]3 [commodity lost]; olives 1¼; olives-TU 1.
HT101.notes: Context: mixed-commodity administrative account, Haghia Triada Casa Room 7, LM IB, HT Scribe 2. GORILA I 166–167 and Younger preserve six lines. A horizontal rule after line 4 separates the lower account. The tablet is substantially abraded and fractured; the lacunae after KU-PA₃-, before 20, and across OLE+KI 2[ / ]3 are grammatically and administratively significant. Younger treats the three upper headings as parallel entities or toponyms; Salgarella and Petrakis (2026, 80–81) classify HT101 among mixed-commodity transfer lists. No KU-RO total is written.

words.note: Hebrew and Aramaic kĕpar 'village', final /r/ unwritten. KA-PA is also quantified elsewhere, so an institution or entity is the rival.
The proposed comparison with Akkadian parsu 'portion, ration' remains an etymological hypothesis; PA alone does not establish the whole phonographic reading.

words.gloss: entry broken before the VIR logogram: GRA+PA 33
words.note: A broad diagonal lacuna crosses lines 2–3. GORILA I 169 reads ]VIR, the line broken before VIR (Younger ]VIR; SigLA VIR).
*dār- 'dwelling, house, granary' + plural -īna; compare DA-RE dāru 'estate'. Rivals: the Amorite place name Dīr, a personal name.
Compare Ugaritic mṯ 'infant' in KTU 1.69:2, 1.5 V:22, and 3.7:15. The final vowel is reconstructed from Linear A, not preserved by alphabetic Ugaritic; MA-ZU is a Linear A hapax.
The arithmetic determines the function: 976 + 33 + 33 + 10 + 3 + 5 = 1,060; including WI 10 would yield 1,070.
KA is dotted. Akkadian ikkaru, Hebrew ʾikkār 'farmer', with unmarked gemination and final /r/ unwritten.

HT102.translation: Village (KA-PA) account: the queen/royal establishment(?)—grain 976; builder/personnel group(?)—GRA+PA grain 33; ]VIR—GRA+PA grain 33; households (DI-RI-NA) 10; MA-ZU 3 (possibly infants or young dependents); 10 excluded/absent; farmer(s) (I-KA) 5. Total: 1,060.
HT102.notes: Damaged administrative grain ledger, Casa Room 7, LM IB, HT Scribe 5. A broad diagonal lacuna crosses lines 2–3. KA-PA is read kapa(r) 'village', MA-ZU maṯu 'infants', I-KA ʾikkār 'farmer'. DI-RI-NA remains untranslated. WI is functionally excluded from the total by exact arithmetic.

HT14.translation: PU-VIN—contribution: grain 30, anointing oil 3, oil (DI) 3, fat(?) 9, olives 13. A-PU₂-NA-DU—grain 47, anointing oil 5, oil (DI) 4, fat(?) 6, olives 14.
HT14.notes:
Context: Two-section commodity allocation—identical commodity sets distributed to two recipients in varying quantities.

Formulaic parallel structure—same five commodities (grain, anointing oil, oil DI, *304, olives) allocated to two different recipients. A-PU₂-NA-DU receives 47 grain against 30, with comparable oil and olive amounts (GORILA I 29). TE between heading and commodities marks the entry as a contribution.

words.note: Contextual comparison with Ugaritic gt /gittu/ 'wine or olive press; farmstead, estate' and Hebrew gat 'press'; a personal or institutional name remains possible.
Its administrative function is supported by repeated oil/liquid contexts; the lexical reading šamnu remains a Semitic identification.
The accounting function is confirmed; the proposed etymology from √k-l-ʾ 'withhold' is secondary. KI-RO 6 is not introduced by KU-RO and is therefore not a summed total.
More exactly PU-*131A, traditionally normalized PU-VIN. It also heads the first allocation section of HT14; no lexical reading is adopted.
GORILA I 211 .6 draws DA (AB01) and TU (AB69): the second sign has TU's crossbars and base, unlike the KI of KI-RO on .2, .5 and .7. The corpus Unicode line agrees (AB01 AB69).

HT123+124a.translation: Press-estate(?)—olives 31; pressed oil 8¼; owed 1 + X (X perhaps ¹⁄₁₂). PU-*131A—olives 31½; pressed oil 8¾; owed X. Šarru (king/prince)—olives 16; pressed oil 4 + A (A701; damaged); owed ¾. DA-TU—olives 15; pressed oil 4¼; owed ¾. Total olives: 93½. Total pressed oil: 25 + H (A706; value disputed). Owed: 6.
HT123+124a.notes: GORILA I, 210–211: olive and oil account on two joining fragments, written over a palimpsest. The clean transcription omits erased signs within the first two KI-RO forms. The olive total is exact: 31 + 31½ + 16 + 15 = 93½. Three securely evaluable *308/OLIV pairs yield approximately 26.6–28.3%; the third *308 fraction is damaged. The final equation relates the disputed A701 (A) and A706 (H) signs but does not establish either value. KI-RO 6 is an outstanding amount, not a KU-RO total.

words.gloss: Pistacia/terebinth oil or related processed product(?)
words.note: The compound combines PROBABLE commodity *188 with the PROBABLE oil/product modifier *308; its exact product name remains hypothetical.
The logogram is tied to textiles by TELA+*312 on HT38; its proposed Semitic name is secondary.

Ugaritic tdt /ṯādīt-/ means 'sixth' (Tropper §§63.113, 63.12). The consonantal sequence is close, but the written vowels do not reproduce Tropper's vocalization. Here TI-DA-TA is followed by a divider, not the numeral 1, so its administrative function remains uncertain.

PI-SA also precedes a CYP+D allocation on KH6, supporting a recipient or institutional name rather than a commodity. Amorite Bu-ṣí (Huffmon 1965, 303), with PI for b and SA for ṣ. Rival: an institution receiving allocations.
The subtype recurs on HTWa1021 and HTWc3020, but the function of DU is unresolved.

GORILA and Younger read AB003 PA; the imported SigLA layer labels the same position AB002 RO. Cash and Cash further note that PA may be confused palaeographically with fraction sign A. No lexical reading is adopted.
The same form heads the aromatic account HT23a. Here a central lacuna follows KA-NA and probably removes its quantity, so the word is not independently identified by this tablet.
HT123b .4 ]SI-DU, beyond the central lacuna that follows KA-NẠ[. The join with HT 124 leaves the lacuna open (GORILA I 210–213). Sole attestation.
No chronologically and morphologically secure Semitic comparison was found.
The function is confirmed corpus-internally; the proposed √k-l-ʾ etymology remains secondary. The amount is broken after 5.

HT123+124b.translation: Pistacia/terebinth oil or processed product(?): 11; flax/linen(?): 1¾. Sixth(?) [section]. Pīsa(?): 4. Pistacia/terebinth product(?): 1. DU-qualified *188 product: 10. TU-PA-DI-DA: J+L2. Sweet cane(?): [quantity lost]. SI-DU: A701. DU-MA-I-NA: ⅜. Total: 20. Owed: 5[…].
HT123+124b.notes: GORILA I, 212–213. The tablet is broken through line 4 after KA-NA, and the missing area probably contained a numerical entry. The divider after TI-DA-TA is not the numeral 1. Under Corazza et al. 2021, J+L2 equals 11/20 and A701 is tentatively 1/24; those authors excluded HT123b itself from their sample because its readings and arithmetic are doubtful. Cash and Cash 2012 explore a three-group account with deductions but require disputed readings and restorations, so their arithmetic model is not adopted here. The closing KU-RO and KI-RO establish a total and an outstanding amount, but the damaged intermediate entries do not permit a complete reconstruction.

Corazza et al. 2021, 8–9: exclusion of HT123b from the reliable sample

words.note: Broken on both sides; no word can be recovered.

words.gloss: KI-type oil; perhaps standard or genuine-grade oil(?)
words.note: The oil subtype is secure. Akkadian kīnu 'true, genuine' supplies a tentative comparison, but no exact ancient oil collocation is known.
Its quantity is lost in the right break. Arabic √ʿ-ṣ-r 'squeeze, press' permits 'pressed oil' only as a tentative comparison; Ugaritic ʿṣr means 'bird' and does not support that reading.

Compare Hebrew šemen ham-mišḥā 'the anointing oil' (Exod 25:6; 29:7; 31:11) and šemen mišḥat qōdeš 'holy anointing oil' (Exod 30:25, 31). MI may be a phonetic complement for mišḥ-, but does not prove the reading.
The group functions elsewhere as an entity or institutional heading. Because the line begins at a break, HT125a cannot independently establish that SA-RA₂ was complete here.
The OLE host is preserved; its following adjunct is damaged.

HT125a.translation: […] KI-type oil: 1⅙; U-type oil: [quantity lost]; anointing or ceremonial oil(?): 1½; […] the queen or royal establishment(?): grain 2; oil-[subtype lost] 1.
HT125a.notes: GORILA I, 214–215 describes the upper part as damaged (sup. mutil.). The inscription is an oil-and-grain account, not continuous prose. Fraction D/A703 is ⅙ under Corazza et al. 2021; J is ½. The commodity subtypes are secure, but their proposed Semitic expansions remain CANDIDATE.

words.note: Only the quantity survives; the associated entry is lost at the upper-left break.

The text preserves only ]RE-TA₂. Younger restores [KI-]RE-TA₂; HT 129 independently preserves KI-RE-TA₂ before the closely matching commodity sequence GRA, *304, NI. The completion is editorial and must remain bracketed.
A distinct grain category is secure; PA does not by itself establish the proposed phonographic expansion parsu.
The compound grain sign is secure. Its exact product is unknown; 'flour' is possible but unproved.

words.gloss: oil/fat-register commodity; perhaps fat or tallow: 10
words.note: Commodity ideogram; the tablet does not identify it as olive oil.

HT125b.notes: GORILA I, 214–215 describes the upper part as damaged. The restoration [KI-]RE-TA₂ is strongly supported by HT 129, whose complete KI-RE-TA₂ heading precedes GRA 33⅔, *304 10, and NI 22, but it is not preserved on HT 125b itself. The surviving quantities total 80½; no KU-RO total survives. Younger tentatively interprets side a as disbursements and side b as contributions. Salgarella and Petrakis classify HT 125b structurally among transfer lists, but this does not determine the direction of transfer or the lexical value of its heading.

words.note: The group is intact but a hapax. Semitic √d-n-s 'be dirty' and Egyptian dns 'be heavy' are formal rather than contextual matches and are not adopted.
Its position and the HT45a/b parallels support an administrative function, not a phonetic reading.
A sign is lost after NA; Younger also considers A-NA-QA because a pebble obscures the trace.
Broken after U; it cannot independently attest the conjunction u.

Probable personal name. Compare Ugaritic alphabetic śdy, annotated as a PN in šmbʿl bn śdy, and syllabic {m}ša-di-ia at Ugarit. The name comparison does not establish the former derivation from Shaddai.
The group begins at a break. Although *49 is elsewhere read semantically as PALM/TREE, HT126a cannot establish a complete U-*49 compound or an initial conjunction.

HT126a.translation: DA-NA-SI [heading]; *318 [administrative sign]. A-NA-[…]: 1; […] ½; Sidiya/Šadiya: 1[…]; […]U-*49: 1; PI[…]; […]62[…]; […]2[…].
HT126a.notes: GORILA I 217 and the photograph show that the right side and lower center are lost; this is a damaged account, not continuous prose. Only SI-DI-JA can presently be identified beyond its administrative role. The initial break before ]U-*49 prevents HT126a from supporting either a complete U-*49 word or the translation 'and palm/tree produce.'

words.note: *305 is securely a counted personnel category, but its exact age, occupation, or status is unknown. The line begins at the broken left edge.
Only the quantity survives.
AB87/TWE functions as a quantified administrative logogram here; its referent remains unresolved.
The source reads the female-sheep logogram OVISf. It is not the homographic syllabographic sign *21F=/ha/. The entry breaks off before its quantity.
The category sign survives between breaks; no quantity is preserved.
TU is provisionally compared with Semitic *ṯawru 'bull' (Ugaritic ṯr /ṯōru/, Biblical Hebrew šōr). Its placement among animal categories supports the comparison, but the line begins at a break.

HT126b.notes: Reverse of HT 126. GORILA I 217 and the photograph show extensive loss along the left and lower edges; the lower field is missing. The text is a fragmentary administrative list rather than continuous prose.

Huehnergard 2012, 42: Ugaritic ṯr /ṯōru/ < *ṯawru 'bull' and Biblical Hebrew šōr

words.note: The group begins at a break and may continue a lost word. NE cannot presently be equated with NI.

GORILA alternatively identifies the initial composite as *629. No divider separates *304+PA from DA-*47-KU. The latter resembles Akkadian damqu 'good, fine' only if *47=/mo/; this remains an internal comparison, not a translation.

HT127a.notes: GORILA I 218–219 and the photograph show extensive loss above and at the word edges. This is a fragmentary administrative list, not continuous prose. The source marks both quantities 1 typographically as uncertain.

words.note: Broken before and dotted (GORILA I 219 .2 ]NẸ 13[). Not readable.
Totals the section b.1–4 and is summed into KU-RO 292 with VIR+*313c, so it counts persons: the sanctuary's personnel. As HT27a TI-NI-TA · *307.
Whole number here, fractions on HT45b (Younger 2023). No reading.
Four sets of six (Younger 2023).
*545 'may designate a group of people' (Younger 2023, citing Schoep 2002, 136–7). Younger's HT 127 transcription reads KI+ME; the images do not decide the second element.
*301 'may refer to people' here (Younger 2023, HT 127b.6).

HT127b.translation: […] […]NE 13[…]. Total, sanctuary personnel (*307): 156. KU 72, men (VIR+*313c) 24, priests(?) (KI+MU) 15, *301 11, [erased: KI+MU 14]. Total 292.
HT127b.notes: KU-RO 292 sums the section total *307 156, KU 72, VIR+*313c 24, KI+MU 15, *301 11 and the erased KI+MU 14 (278 + 14): the scribe totalled before erasing (Younger 2023: 'KU-RO 292 totals b.4–6, including b.4 KU-RO 156 and the erasure in b.6'). On the photo and facsimile the erased entry survives only as traces.

words.note: QE-TU writes qaṭun 'small' (Heb. qāṭōn), the final n unwritten; cf. QE-TU-NE (HT 12). Rival: Ug. qṭ 'flax'.
Personnel-category logogram (HT89, HT100). No quantity here—a heading for the following allocations.

words.note: *304 compares with Central Semitic *pidr- 'fat' (Heb. peder), distinct from OLE olive oil.

Prepositional allocation: RE = le- 'to, for' (CONFIRMED) before *304 commodity logogram. Specifies a second fat allocation or designates the fat account. Ugaritic parallel: l-ḫpṯ 'for the haruspex' in KTU 4.149.
PS *matn- 'loins' (Heb. māṯnayim). Weak points: MI for ma, DA for t. Rival: a heading or title before PA-JA.
Egyptian Pꜣjj, the first element of PA-JA-RE (HT 8b, 29, 88, ZA 10b). Rival: a Semitic hypocoristic. One attestation.
